clue.text: Hazel perhaps with time to pursue copper engraving (7)

indicators.note: to pursue is to chase, and a chaser comes behind, so time's letter follows copper's

blocks.note: hazel is one kind of wood, hence 'perhaps'
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

explanation.surface: A craftsman works on a copper engraving, perhaps with a hazel handle, taking his time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hazel' looks like a colour or a name; here it is a tree, so its timber is WOOD.
explanation.definitionFit: A woodcut is a print made by engraving a design on a block of wood.

clue.text: Tory’s feverishness after Bill through finally (7,5)

indicators.note: AGUE is placed after the rest
take the last letter of 'through'

blocks.note: ague = a fever with shivering fits

explanation.surface: A Conservative politician is running a temperature after a bill has passed.
explanation.walkthrough: William Hague is a former leader of the Conservative (Tory) party in Britain. 'Bill' reads as parliamentary legislation, but it is the nickname for William.
explanation.definitionFit: William Hague led the Conservative Party, so he is a Tory.

clue.text: External equipment hasn’t drained totally (8)

indicators.note: a word drained of its contents keeps only its outside letters

blocks.note: a rig is a set of equipment

explanation.surface: Someone complains that the outside tank or apparatus hasn't fully emptied.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drained totally' looks like one phrase, but 'drained' works on 'hasn't' and 'totally' stands alone as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Outright can mean completely, as in 'rejected outright'.

clue.text: Committee really upset initially by crucial point (4)

indicators.note: take the first letters of the words before it

blocks.note: first letters of Committee Really Upset
x = by, as in 3 x 4 or a 2-by-4

explanation.surface: A committee is really upset at the start by a crucial issue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'By' looks like a link word; it is the multiplication sign X, as in a room 'ten by twelve'.
explanation.definitionFit: The crux is the decisive or most important point of a matter.

clue.text: Sway social media user to ignore weight (6)

indicators.note: leave the W for weight out

explanation.surface: Someone tries to sway an online influencer into disregarding their weight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sway' reads as a verb of persuasion, but here it means to wobble.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both words describe an unsteady to-and-fro wobble, as of someone on the brink.

clue.text: Dance that is very easy to perform (8)

definitions.note: the second definition describes a task; cakewalk is the noun for such a task

blocks.note: a strutting dance from the American South, once rewarded with a cake
informal for any task done without effort

explanation.surface: A dance that anyone can do without effort.
explanation.walkthrough: The easy-task sense grew out of the dance, which looked effortless.
explanation.definitionFit: A cakewalk is both a dance and something very easily done.

clue.text: Depart, still lacking energy (4)

indicators.note: the word goes without the E

explanation.surface: Someone leaves while still short of energy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Still' reads as an adverb meaning 'even now', but it is the adjective meaning calm.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the sense of leaving a place, as in 'quit the room'.

clue.text: Evening containing a signal for person moved away from danger (7)

indicators.note: EVE holds the other letters

blocks.note: a cue is a signal to act

explanation.surface: An evening alert tells someone to leave for safety.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Evening' looks like a time of the evacuation; it is only EVE.
explanation.definitionFit: An evacuee is someone moved out of a dangerous place.

clue.text: Gemstone with fresh colour (7,5)

blocks.note: an emerald is a precious stone
green = fresh, new, as in green wood

explanation.surface: A gemstone with a bright new colour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fresh colour' reads as one phrase, but 'fresh' is GREEN and 'colour' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by category: the answer names one particular shade, the vivid tint of the gem.

clue.text: Vegetable cutlet prepared first in eatery (7)

indicators.note: the letters are rearranged, as food is prepared
take the first letter of 'eatery'

explanation.surface: At a restaurant, a vegetable cutlet is served as a starter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vegetable cutlet' reads as one dish; 'Vegetable' is the definition and 'cutlet' the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by category: the answer is one salad leaf among many garden crops.

clue.text: Where to see actors taking part in Goethe? At rehearsal (7)

indicators.note: the answer is part of the following letters

explanation.surface: Asking where actors perform a Goethe play in rehearsal.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as a question about actors in a Goethe play, which neatly also describes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A descriptive definition: the answer is the building or stage where plays are performed.

clue.text: Part of river Thames one’s seen repeatedly (4)

indicators.note: 'repeatedly' means again and again, so the chunk it follows appears a second time

blocks.note: one = the Roman numeral; the apostrophe-s is the verb 'is'
the same chunk a second time

explanation.surface: A stretch of the Thames that keeps turning up.
explanation.walkthrough: The Isis is the name for the Thames as it flows through Oxford. 'One's' reads as a possessive, but it is I + 'S (is).
explanation.definitionFit: The Isis is the stretch of the Thames around Oxford.

clue.text: Fish a French duke recalled on Hebridean island (9)

indicators.note: called back, so the letters run backwards
the reversed part comes after the island

blocks.note: Barra is an island in the Outer Hebrides

explanation.surface: A French duke goes fishing and is summoned home from a Scottish island.
explanation.walkthrough: The Hebrides are islands off the west coast of Scotland. 'Recalled' sounds like a summons home, but it reverses A DUC to CUDA.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by category: the answer is one predatory, sharp-toothed sea species.

clue.text: Middle Eastern graduate welcome to grab shower (8)

indicators.note: to grab something is to seize and hold it, so the greeting's letters hold the shower's

blocks.note: a shower is a spell of rain

explanation.surface: A graduate from the Middle East is welcomed and grabs a shower.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shower' suggests washing, but it is weather.
explanation.definitionFit: Bahraini describes something or someone from Bahrain, in the Middle East.

clue.text: Dicky puts melodies in one’s head (8)

indicators.note: dicky = faulty, unsound, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone foolish gets tunes stuck in their head.
explanation.walkthrough: Dicky is British slang for weak or unreliable, as in a dicky heart. 'Upstairs' is informal for the mind, as in 'not much upstairs'.
explanation.definitionFit: Informally, upstairs means in the head or mind: 'he's not all there upstairs'.

clue.text: Car reversed behind plot (9)

indicators.note: swap the order of the two words that follow

blocks.note: to hatch a plot is to scheme

explanation.surface: A car backing up behind a garden plot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reversed' suggests reading letters backwards, but here it flips the order of whole words: 'behind plot' becomes plot + behind.
explanation.definitionFit: A hatchback is a car with a rear door that opens upwards.

clue.text: Beating path, robber hides (6)

indicators.note: the answer is concealed in the words before it

explanation.surface: A robber lies hidden by a path after beating someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beating' reads as an assault in the surface, but here it describes a pounding heart.
explanation.definitionFit: Athrob means throbbing, beating rhythmically.

clue.text: Male’s small identifying mark (4)

blocks.note: s = small, as on clothing labels

explanation.surface: A man's little name tag.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's reads as a possessive but is 'is', linking definition to wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A stag is a male deer, and 'stag' means men-only, as in a stag party.

clue.text: Giant pig restricts dog heading west (7)

indicators.note: to restrict is to hem in, so the pig's letters fence the dog's in
in an across clue, going west means reading right to left

blocks.note: to dog or tail someone is to follow them

explanation.surface: An enormous pig keeps a dog from roaming west.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dog' looks like a second animal beside the pig, but it is the verb meaning to follow someone.
explanation.definitionFit: Goliath was the biblical giant, and the name now means any giant.

clue.text: Regularly flaunt unknown ice-skating jump (4)

indicators.note: 'regularly' means at even intervals, so letters are taken at every other position

blocks.note: algebra uses x, y and z for unknowns

explanation.surface: A skater keeps showing off an unfamiliar jump.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unknown' seems to describe the jump; it is the algebra letter Z.
explanation.definitionFit: A lutz is a figure-skating jump taken off from the back outside edge.

clue.text: 50 per cent of judges love sport (4)

indicators.note: 50 per cent is a half, so only half the word's letters survive

blocks.note: love = zero, O, as in tennis scores

explanation.surface: Half the judging panel love this sport.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is a statistic about judges' tastes; 'love' is the tennis zero.
explanation.definitionFit: Judo is a Japanese martial art practised as a sport.

clue.text: Ordinary path around home (7)

indicators.note: 'around' means encircling, so the path's letters surround the other chunk

explanation.surface: A normal walk around the house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Home' reads as a place; here it is IN, as in 'staying in'.
explanation.definitionFit: Routine can mean ordinary, run-of-the-mill.

clue.text: Half of each can to corrode (3,4)

indicators.note: take half the letters of 'each'

explanation.surface: Half the cans are starting to rust.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Can' reads as a verb ('able to'), but it is the container, TIN.
explanation.definitionFit: A phrasal-verb synonym: acid gradually wears metal away, which is what rust does too.

clue.text: British eccentric adopts American attire (7)

definitions.note: attire is a general word for clothing; a blouson is one garment

indicators.note: to adopt is to take someone into your family, so the eccentric takes the American inside

blocks.note: a loon is an eccentric or crazy person

explanation.surface: An eccentric Briton takes to dressing like an American.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Eccentric' looks like an anagram indicator but is the noun LOON.
explanation.definitionFit: A blouson is a short jacket gathered at the waist, an item of attire.
